findings.finding: New tests exercise nested-form exclusion and one intended POST with no composer submit/draft loss. They do not exercise native dialog close/cancel focus restoration or standalone body fallback. showModal/close are simplified stubs and close does not dispatch close.
findings.recommendation: Keep these lifecycle/fallback cases explicit as not verified by these two tests. Existing real-browser evidence can cover them if it includes those actions; do not infer native focus behavior from jsdom stubs.

findings.finding: Build regenerated tracked derived outputs with broad changes beyond the seven-line source diff. dist/index.html now names new hashed assets while git tracks no assets in that directory. This is an artifact/publication-scope observation, not a newly demonstrated source regression.
findings.recommendation: Choose deliberately whether derived artifacts belong in the PR; avoid publishing a changed bare dist index as a standalone frontend without its built assets.

positive_findings: Portal removes the actual HTML dialog/forms from the composer form while preserving normal .control-chat ancestor styling.
onSubmit stopPropagation is necessary because React portal events can reach logical React ancestors even when DOM form ancestry is removed.
KnowledgeIngest own submit handler retains preventDefault and its intended fetch; no payload/provider selection logic changed.
Normal open state transition after selecting a resource rerenders the portal into the closest .control-chat before the effect calls showModal on the new dialog ref.
Close/cancel handlers and launcher focus callback are preserved; dialog and resource-specific global CSS remain applicable. No new functional defect found in these paths by static reasoning.

When rendered with no .control-chat ancestor in a browser, the dialog targets document.body and remains outside a surrounding form. SSR without document is not supported by this new render path; current app is CSR/Vite.
The two added tests assert observable behavior and fail the original nested-form conditions rather than mirroring implementation details alone.
